title: Prisma ORM
definition: A next-generation Object-Relational Mapper (ORM) for Node.js and TypeScript, used heavily in the Next.js ecosystem to interact with databases securely.
simpleExplanation: Instead of writing complex, messy raw SQL strings like `SELECT * FROM users WHERE age > 18`, Prisma lets you write clean, auto-completed JavaScript code like `prisma.user.findMany({ where: { age: { gt: 18 } } })`.
realWorldExample: Using Prisma to define a `User` model, push that schema to a PostgreSQL database to create the actual tables, and then using the generated Prisma Client inside a Next.js Server Component to fetch the users.

basic: What file extension is used for the main Prisma configuration file where you define your database schema?
intermediate: Why does Next.js 14 pair incredibly well with Prisma compared to older React architectures?

answers.question: Why pairs well?
answers.answer: Because of Server Components. You can literally import the Prisma Client directly into a React component file and query the database right next to your HTML output. No need to build an entire backend API.
